predictions.title: Unsloth ships full agent-loader mitigation as a fine-tuning default by H2 2026
predictions.body: By H2 2026 Unsloth ships the complete five-surface agent-loader mitigation set as the on-by-default behavior of its local-LLM fine-tuning stack, holding the first-mover position it has carried since the disclosure wave and making it the reference open-source training stack that already conforms to the consolidated loader-verification baseline the agentic-AI framework cohort will adopt mid-June. The Sunday catalysts are concrete and converge on a settled reference rather than a fresh feature surface. Unsloth's Sunday changelog ships a small weekend stability fix to the multi-GPU NCCL backend for the router-only LoRA recipe, closing a rank-imbalance edge case in the tensor-parallel router-attention all-reduce, and explicitly confirms Unsloth continues to carry the full five-surface coverage — load-time signed-checkpoint, manifest-allowlist with the nested-dependency-resolution canonicalization extension, workflow-state path-canonicalization, and intermediate-state-serializer canonicalization — holding its first-mover status as the local-LLM fine-tuning stack carrying the full set ahead of the LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, Haystack, and Pydantic AI maintainer cohort's coordinated mid-June default-shipment target. A Sunday Hugging Face Blog post logs the router-only LoRA recipe's NCCL backend as stable across the full single-node multi-GPU tier from dual-RTX-5090 consumer setups to octa-Hopper workstations, and a contributor documents the community DeepSeek R3-Pro 38B Mixture-of-Experts recipe completing a dual-card consumer router-only run at roughly 6 percent peak combined VRAM with the mitigation set intact, drawing an eighth Hacker News reproduction. Reinforcing the timing, the Sunday arxiv 2605.07412 empirical-evaluation note pairs the Saturday unified five-surface formal model with a reproduction study and a per-surface micro-benchmark showing the signed-checkpoint and manifest-allowlist paths add only a low single-digit-percentage agent cold-start overhead, supplying the measured-overhead budget that makes always-on the defensible default. The structural force is that once the five-surface mitigation set is the documented reference the framework cohort has publicly tied its mid-June default to, the verification overhead is measured and small, and Unsloth already carries the full set across the entire consumer-to-workstation tier with a stable multi-GPU backend, Unsloth cannot ship an H2 2026 release keeping any surface opt-in without forfeiting the first-mover conformance lead its changelogs have repeatedly claimed. The most likely landing is an H2 2026 Unsloth release documenting all five mitigation surfaces as the default for both LoRA and router-only recipes across the consumer-to-octa-Hopper tier, citing the consolidated arxiv reference and its measured-overhead budget, ahead of or in step with the framework cohort's mid-June default-shipment wave. Bear case is that Unsloth keeps the intermediate-state-serializer surface behind an opt-in flag for a recipe-compatibility window and defaults only four surfaces; absent that carve-out, H2 2026 lands the full five-surface agent-loader mitigation as the Unsloth fine-tuning-stack default.

predictions.summary: Sunday's Unsloth changelog reaffirms it still carries the full five-surface agent-loader mitigation set ahead of the framework cohort's mid-June default, and a fresh arxiv note measures the verification overhead as small. By H2 2026 Unsloth ships all five surfaces as its fine-tuning-stack default.

predictions.title: Alphabet breaks out AI Services revenue in a dedicated 10-Q footnote by Q4 2026
predictions.body: By Q4 2026 Alphabet discloses a dedicated AI Services revenue line in a 10-Q footnote, formalizing the disaggregated AI-revenue breakout that the sell-side print-cycle cohort has spent the cycle pricing as near-certain and setting the segment-disclosure template that the rest of the Mag-7 prints follow into the same window. The Sunday catalysts are concrete and span the analyst consensus, the catalyst calendar, and the regulatory backdrop. A Sunday 247 Wall St note reports the print-cycle preview cohort — Bernstein, Wells Fargo Securities, Evercore ISI, Citi Research, Jefferies, and Goldman Sachs Equity Research — holding the Alphabet Q2 AI Services 10-Q footnote breakout probability at 87 percent, with the May 21 Alphabet analyst day stepping to T-minus-four calendar days and the cohort naming Monday's open as the start of the analyst-day run-up window. The cohort is treating the Friday SEC Corp Fin fourth sample comment letter on AI-services-revenue measurement basis and the four-consecutive-day Cerebras consolidation as settled pricing inputs, meaning the disclosure question has shifted from whether to the exact footnote shape. A Sunday VentureBeat aggregation reiterates the cohort consensus that Microsoft, Meta, and AWS ship their own AI Services revenue breakout in their fiscal Q3 2026 prints, with the Alphabet-led Q4 2026 print cadence unchanged — placing Alphabet as the cadence-setter the sibling prints track. The structural force is that once a six-desk preview cohort has converged at an 87 percent breakout probability, the SEC has issued a fourth sample comment letter establishing an AI-services-revenue measurement-basis disclosure precedent, and the sibling Mag-7 names are already expected to mirror the breakout in adjacent fiscal-quarter prints, Alphabet cannot hold an analyst day and report through Q4 2026 without a disaggregated AI Services footnote and still stay inside the disclosure norm its own peers are converging on. The most likely landing is Alphabet publishing a dedicated AI Services revenue footnote in a 2026 10-Q no later than Q4 2026, with a stated measurement basis responsive to the Corp Fin sample-letter precedent, and at least two of Microsoft, Meta, and AWS shipping a comparable breakout in their adjacent fiscal-Q3 prints. Bear case is that Alphabet's analyst day offers only qualitative AI-revenue color and defers the formal footnote to a fiscal-year filing past Q4 2026; absent that deferral, Q4 2026 lands the dedicated AI Services revenue footnote as an Alphabet 10-Q disclosure.

predictions.title: Frontier Model Review Board executive order is signed into effect by Q3 2026
predictions.body: By Q3 2026 the Frontier Model Review Board executive order is signed and takes effect, carrying the AISI cyber-evaluation reciprocity 120-day placement window and the per-state attorney-general consultation pathway intact, and tying the United States into the cross-jurisdiction cyber-evaluation reciprocity perimeter that has otherwise hardened around fifteen named candidates without it. The Sunday catalysts are concrete and trace a clearing-blocker sequence. A Sunday Just Security weekend reading reaffirms that the Friday unclassified summary memo's no-objection finding on the per-state attorney-general consultation pathway and the AISI cyber-evaluation reciprocity 120-day placement window removes the principal cited signing-window blocker, while White House OSTP holds that the order remains in interagency review with no signing window before May 22. A Sunday Lawfare procedural note reports the Senate Cyber Subcommittee's classified-annex follow-up question set, transmitted Friday to the eight-witness slate, drawing early acknowledgement of receipt from NIST Director Locascio's office and the CISA Director's office, with substantive responses due when the ten-business-day clock expires — placing the last procedural gate on a defined, near-term calendar. The House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee's parallel 30-day technical-review joint-resolution draft continues circulating for markup scheduling. The structural force is that once the substantive policy blocker is cleared by a no-objection finding, the remaining classified-annex question set is on a fixed ten-business-day clock, OSTP itself has named a concrete post-May-22 signing window rather than an open-ended hold, and the cross-jurisdiction reciprocity perimeter has already reached fifteen named candidates plus the originating UK and EU while the US recognition gap stays open, the order's signing compresses to interagency-clock arithmetic — annex responses plus a short interagency-clearance interval lands the signature inside Q3 2026. The most likely landing is the Frontier Model Review Board executive order signed and effective in Q3 2026 with the AISI cyber-evaluation reciprocity 120-day placement window and the per-state attorney-general consultation pathway intact as cleared by the no-objection finding, the classified-annex responses filed on the ten-business-day clock, and the order cited as the instrument that begins closing the US recognition gap against the fifteen-jurisdiction reciprocity perimeter. Bear case is that an adverse classified-annex response or the House joint-resolution markup reopens substantive review and pushes the signing into Q4 2026; absent that reopening, Q3 2026 lands the Frontier Model Review Board executive order signed into effect.

reasoning.given: OSTP named a post-May-22 signing window and the annex questions sit on a 10-business-day clock.
reasoning.so_that: The Frontier Model Review Board executive order is signed and takes effect, with reciprocity terms intact.
reasoning.landing: By Q3 2026; the FMRB order signed, annex responses filed on the clock.
reasoning.plain_language: The main obstacle to the US frontier-AI oversight order is gone, so the President is likely to sign it within a few months.

predictions.summary: Friday's no-objection finding removed the principal blocker to the Frontier Model Review Board executive order, OSTP named a post-May-22 signing window, and the last classified-annex questions sit on a fixed clock. By Q3 2026 the order is signed and takes effect with its reciprocity terms intact.
